profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the research lead for an LLM MLOps optimization project and the systems engineer integrating the evaluation pipeline before an internal demo and paper artifact freeze. The team has already agreed on the headline framework design, and this meeting is meant to align interfaces and handoffs across the modeling and infrastructure workstreams: what results package will be delivered, which deployment traces are included in the final benchmark run, how the adaptive controller will be wired into the shared orchestration repo, and what 'ready for demo' means by the end of the week. The agenda is to confirm the benchmark bundle, the controller handoff, the resource budget assumptions for the multi-cloud runs, and ownership of the final results tables. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on who will provide the controller outputs, who will execute the replay runs, and what artifact will be used in the demo and paper appendix.

members.name: Dr. Maya Chen
members.expertise: LLM systems evaluation, learned schedulers, experimental design for ML systems
members.background: Maya leads the research side of the project and designed the DNN-based policy that predicts deployment and resource allocation decisions from operational telemetry; she is focused on producing publishable, reproducible benchmark results across several cloud settings.
members.private_state: She wants the final benchmark package to preserve comparability with the experiments already used in the draft paper, avoid reopening evaluation logic this late, and ensure the demo reflects the polished offline results rather than a potentially noisy live integration.
hidden_assumptions: The 'benchmark bundle' refers to the curated replay dataset and configs used for the paper tables, not raw production traces or live traffic replays.

When the team says the controller is 'integrated,' that means its decisions are exported in the agreed JSON schema and consumed by the orchestrator shim, not that the learning loop is running online in the cluster.
A run being 'ready' means the summary tables and plots match the target deltas within expected variance and are reproducible from the frozen artifact commit.
The 'multi-cloud run' means the three cloud environments already standardized in the draft experiments, each under the capped quota profile used in prior evaluations.

members.name: Arjun Patel
members.expertise: Kubernetes-based ML deployment, inference platform orchestration, CI/CD for large-scale model serving
members.background: Arjun owns the deployment pipeline and shared orchestration repository where the adaptive controller will be hooked into the serving stack; he focuses on operational realism, maintainability, and making the demo path look like the production path.
members.private_state: He wants to minimize custom one-off evaluation code, avoid being responsible for manually curating paper-only artifacts, and make sure the demo uses the actual integrated control path so the infrastructure team can reuse it after the research milestone.
hidden_assumptions: The 'benchmark bundle' means the packaged set of deployment traces and manifests pulled from the latest sanitized production export, because that is the only bundle the infra team treats as canonical.

When people say the controller is 'integrated,' they mean it is running through the orchestrator's callback interface inside the deployment service, even if learning is disabled and only inference is active.
A system being 'ready' means it can be triggered from the shared pipeline, complete a full end-to-end run without manual patching, and write outputs to the team artifact bucket.

The 'multi-cloud run' means replaying across all currently supported cluster profiles, including the newly added spot-heavy GCP profile that the platform team now considers part of the standard matrix.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the benchmark bundle
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to 'the benchmark bundle' as the thing that will be handed off for final runs.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the frozen paper evaluation package: curated workload replays, fixed configs, and the exact cloud/profile subset used to generate the draft results.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the latest sanitized production-derived bundle from the infra artifact store, which includes newer manifests and an expanded workload mix.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both teams already use the same label internally, and because each bundle is a legitimate packaged artifact with manifests and traces, neither expects ambiguity when discussing a handoff.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that 'the controller will be integrated by Thursday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the controller will output decisions in the stable JSON interface and the orchestrator shim will read them during replay experiments.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the controller inference service will be wired into the orchestrator callback path used by the deployment pipeline so end-to-end jobs invoke it directly.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'integrated' sounds complete and standard to both of them, and both interpretations are plausible late-stage forms of integration that stop short of discussing architecture details explicitly.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say the system should be 'ready for demo' by end of week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'ready for demo' means the frozen artifact can reproduce the headline improvement tables and a polished replay can be shown reliably.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'ready for demo' means a user can launch the job from the shared CI/deployment pipeline and observe the controller drive a complete run without ad hoc intervention.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both criteria are reasonable forms of readiness for a research demo, and because the meeting is about coordination rather than acceptance testing, they never enumerate the pass conditions.

misalignment_points.topic: Scope of the standard multi-cloud run
misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on doing 'the standard multi-cloud run' before freeze.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 includes AWS, Azure, and the previously approved on-demand GCP setup under fixed quota caps matching the draft study.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 includes all currently standard platform profiles, including the newly added spot-heavy GCP configuration used by the infra team for cost-sensitive validation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Calling something the 'standard' matrix implies settled boundaries, so neither feels a need to restate the exact profiles, especially since both assume they are simply referring to the current default set.
